concepts.title: Cabling a Mesh Topology
concepts.definition: In a mesh topology every communicating device links to every other one, which makes the network reliable and secure but expensive, because n nodes need n times n minus 1 over 2 separate cables.
concepts.key_idea: Five nodes in a full mesh already need ten wires, and the count grows quadratically.
question_patterns: How many cables are needed to build a fully connected mesh of 5 nodes?
A mesh network must serve 10 nodes. Compute the number of wires required.
Why does mesh topology handle heavy traffic and node failures better than others?
State two drawbacks of the mesh topology.
How many new cables are added when a sixth node joins a five-node mesh?

solution_steps.explain: Each of n nodes could link to n minus 1 others.
A to B and B to A share one cable.

worked_examples.q: How many cables does a full mesh of 5 nodes need?

concepts.title: File Transfer over a Gigabit LAN
concepts.definition: A LAN transfers data at rates from 10 Mbps (Ethernet) up to 1000 Mbps (Gigabit Ethernet); the time to move a file is its size in megabits divided by the transfer rate in megabits per second.
concepts.key_idea: A 700 MB file crosses a Gigabit Ethernet in about 5.6 seconds, but needs 560 seconds on plain 10 Mbps Ethernet.
question_patterns: How long does a 700 MB file take to move across a Gigabit Ethernet running at 1000 Mbps?
The same file travels over 10 Mbps Ethernet. Compute the transfer time in seconds.
Expand the abbreviation Mbps and state the LAN speed range it appears in.
Up to what distance can a LAN be extended, and which areas does it cover?
Why is a LAN considered comparatively secure?

solution_steps.explain: Seconds equal megabits split by megabits per second.

worked_examples.q: A 700 MB file crosses a Gigabit Ethernet rated at 1000 Mbps. About how many seconds does it take?

concepts.title: Bit Structure of a MAC Address
concepts.definition: A MAC address is the permanent hardware address engraved on a NIC: it has 12 hexadecimal digits equal to 48 bits, split evenly into a 24-bit manufacturer identifier called the OUI and a 24-bit serial number.
concepts.key_idea: The first six hex digits name the manufacturer and the last six identify the individual card.
question_patterns: How many bits long is a MAC address, and how many hexadecimal digits does it use?
How many bits carry the Organisational Unique Identifier, and what does OUI stand for?
Why can a MAC address never be changed?
How does a MAC address differ from an IP address in permanence?
Split a 48-bit MAC address into its two 24-bit halves and name each part.

solution_steps.explain: The manufacturer identifier takes the first half of the bits.

worked_examples.q: How many bits long is a MAC address?

concepts.title: Address Space of IPv4
concepts.definition: An IPv4 address is a 32-bit number written as four decimal numbers from 0 to 255 separated by dots; 32 bits allow just under 4.3 billion distinct addresses, which is why the 128-bit IPv6 with eight hexadecimal groups was proposed.
concepts.key_idea: Two raised to 32 gives about 4.29 billion addresses, too few for today's connected devices.
question_patterns: How many unique addresses does the 32-bit IPv4 scheme offer, approximately?
Write the sample IPv4 address given in the chapter and describe its four parts.
How is an IPv6 address written, and how many bits does it use?
Why was IPv6 proposed when IPv4 already existed?
Which address can change when a device moves to another network: MAC or IP, and why?

solution_steps.explain: Divide by one billion to compare with the chapter's figure.

worked_examples.q: How many bits does an IPv4 address carry?

concepts.title: Network Types: PAN, LAN, MAN and WAN
concepts.definition: Networks are classified by the area they cover: PAN links personal devices within about 10 metres, LAN covers a room to a campus up to 1 km at 10 to 1000 Mbps, MAN spans a city of 30 to 40 km, and WAN connects cities, countries and continents, with the Internet as the largest WAN.
concepts.formula: PAN 10 m -> LAN 1 km -> MAN 40 km -> WAN global
concepts.key_idea: Cable TV networks illustrate a MAN, while two phones on Bluetooth form a wireless PAN.
question_patterns: Which network type connects devices within a 10 metre range, and give one wired and one wireless example.
Two universities in different states want to share information. Which network type do they need?
Differentiate LAN and WAN on coverage and data rate.
Name two examples of a Metropolitan Area Network.
Why is the Internet called the largest WAN?
Which network category covers a school campus, and which cable speeds does it usually run at?

solution_steps.action: match the area to the type
solution_steps.explain: Place the coverage and speed of the situation against the four categories; the smallest personal range is PAN and the globe-spanning one is WAN.

worked_examples.q: Which network type links personal devices within about 10 metres?

concepts.title: Devices: Modem, Hub, Switch, Router and Gateway
concepts.definition: Each network device has a distinct job: a modem converts between digital bits and analog signals, a repeater regenerates weak signals, a hub broadcasts incoming data to all lines, a switch forwards packets only to the addressed device, a router connects and routes between networks, and a gateway is the entry and exit point of a network.
concepts.formula: modem: digital <-> analog; switch: selective; router: between networks
concepts.key_idea: Unlike a hub, a switch reads the destination address in the packet and drops corrupted signals instead of passing them on.
question_patterns: What does the word modem stand for, and what conversion does it perform?
How does a switch differ from a hub in forwarding data?
Explain the working of a repeater and state the usual cable distance it serves.
Why is a router considered more capable than a hub or a switch?
What is a gateway, and which device is usually configured to act as one at home?
Name the connector used with Ethernet cables and the card it plugs into.

solution_steps.action: match the job to the device
solution_steps.explain: Identify what the situation needs, signal conversion, regeneration, broadcasting, selective forwarding, inter-network routing, or the network boundary, and pick the device built for it.

worked_examples.q: Which device converts between digital bits and analog signals?

concepts.title: Comparing Ring, Bus, Star and Tree Topologies
concepts.definition: Ring connects each node to two neighbours so data travels one way around the loop; bus shares one backbone wire among all nodes; star wires every node to a central hub or switch; and tree or hybrid joins several basic topologies under a hierarchy.
concepts.formula: ring: 2 links per node; bus: 1 shared wire; star: 1 link to centre
concepts.key_idea: A failed central device brings down a whole star network, while a bus failure splits the line.
question_patterns: Identify the topology: one single cable shared by all nodes; each node wired to a central switching device.
How is tree topology different from bus topology?
Why are bus and ring considered less secure and less reliable than star?
What happens in a star network when the central hub fails?
In which direction can data move in a ring topology?
Which topology joins several star networks over a bus, and where is it usually realised?

solution_steps.explain: Count how many ways each node connects, one shared wire, two neighbours, one centre, or many branches, and that decides the topology name.

worked_examples.q: Which topology wires every node to a central hub or switch?

concepts.title: Internet, Web and Domain Name System
concepts.definition: The Internet is the global network of devices, while the World Wide Web is the collection of interlinked pages served over it using HTML, URL and HTTP; because numeric addresses are hard to remember, a DNS server resolves each domain name to its IP address.
concepts.formula: domain name -> DNS server -> IP address
concepts.key_idea: Entering www.ncert.nic.in makes the browser ask a DNS server, which answers with 164.100.60.233.
question_patterns: Distinguish the World Wide Web from the Internet with one example of each.
Name the three technologies through which Tim Berners-Lee created the web.
What is a URL and how does it differ from a domain name?
What is a DNS server, and what is domain name resolution?
Which protocol fetches a web page, and which is its more secure version?
Expand ARPANET, MAC, ISP and URI.
From Table 10.1, which IP address belongs to wikipedia.org?

solution_steps.action: follow a URL through the resolver
solution_steps.explain: The browser hands the domain name to a DNS server, receives the matching IP address, and then HTTP retrieves the page from that server.

worked_examples.q: Which server resolves a domain name into its IP address?

worked_examples.title: Wires for a six-node mesh
worked_examples.problem: A laboratory wants a full mesh of 6 computers. Compute the number of cables needed.

steps.explain: Each unordered pair shares one cable.

worked_examples.answer_note: The mesh needs 15 cables, matching the formula n(n-1)/2.
